description: Spread a T-12, operating statement, budget or rent roll summary YOU read, onto FactLot's published chart of accounts (multifamily, commercial, or hotel after the USALI summary), deterministically; FactLot runs no model. Send the pages as text and one line per item: {label, amount, quote, page}, optionally your category, a period column, and for a subtotal the indexes of the lines it sums; give the statement's own totals (effective_gross_income, total_operating_expenses, net_operating_income, ebitda, ...) as lines with that total as category. Each line is checked: the quote is on the page (a quote under 12 characters, such as a short row, only where it stands as whole words), the amount (as a number, any common written form; (1,200) and -1,200 read as negative) and the label are written in it; a line that fails is excluded with the reason, and a stated total that does not foot names the lines left out. The label is mapped to the chart by keywords: your category is used when it is in the chart, and an exception flags it for review when the dictionary maps the label elsewhere; an ambiguous or unknown label without a category is excluded. Vacancy, concessions, credit loss and other contra lines are always subtracted. Returns per period the sections, the computed totals (EGI, operating expenses, NOI, capital items, net cash flow; for hotels departmental profit, GOP, EBITDA and NOI after the replacement reserve), whether each total and subtotal the statement states foots (within 0.5 per line added, or your tolerance), every line with its citation (document, page, quote, span) and status, statistics (units, occupancy, ADR), and exceptions to review. Not checked: whether the agent missed lines, and meaning beyond the written amount and label.

ocr_pages.description: Optional: pages (1-based) whose text came from OCR rather than the file's text layer (doc_read_pdf and factlot.read_pdf report them). Facts and citations on these pages carry ocr: true, so a reviewer checks the scan.

pages.description: The document's text, one string per page in order: pages[0] is page 1. Send the text as extracted (from the PDF text layer or OCR), not a summary; quotes are matched against it.

items.description: The text of one page, exactly as extracted.

sha256.description: Optional SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the original file. When given, document_id is fl:document:sha256-<this>, the same ID id_document gives the file; FactLot cannot check that the pages came from that file. Without it, document_id is the SHA-256 of the pages joined by form feeds (\f).

title.description: Document title for citations, e.g. "First Amendment to Lease".

lines.description: The statement's lines as you read them: every income, expense and capital line, the statement's own subtotals (with sums) and totals (with a total category), and statistics such as units or occupancy.

amount.description: The amount as a plain number (245000, not "$245K"). Write a deduction as the statement shows it; vacancy, concessions and other contra lines are always subtracted.

category.description: Your proposed category from the chart for property_type (spec/schemas/vocabularies/chart-of-accounts.json), e.g. real_estate_taxes, or a total such as net_operating_income for a total line. Without it, FactLot maps the label itself.

label.description: The line's label exactly as the statement writes it, e.g. "Real Estate Taxes". It must appear in the quote.

period.description: Period column the amount is from, e.g. "T-12 Sep 2026" or "2025". Lines are spread per period. Default: the statement's period.

quote.description: Verbatim text from the page with the label and the amount, e.g. "Real Estate Taxes 245,000". A row shorter than 12 characters ("R&M 310,411") is accepted where it appears on the page as whole words.

sums.description: For a subtotal the statement prints ("Total Utilities"): the indexes (0-based) of the lines it adds up. FactLot checks that it foots.

period.description: Default period label for lines that give none.

property_type.description: Which chart of accounts to use: multifamily, commercial (office, retail, industrial), or hotel (USALI summary).

statement_type.description: What the document is; echoed back.

tolerance.description: Largest difference, in the statement's units, at which a subtotal or total still foots. Default: 0.5 for each line added (rounding).

name: doc_spread_statement
title: Spread an operating statement
